question: What is the product of all the solutions to the equation \[ \begin{gathered} \log_{7x}2023\cdot\log_{289x}2023\\ {}=\log_{2023x}2023? \end{gathered} \]
solution:
The identity \(2023=7\cdot289\) makes the constants add to \(1\) when all logarithms are written in base \(2023\). This will cancel the linear term after a substitution.

All logarithm bases must be positive and different from \(1\), so \(x>0\). Define
\[
a=\log_{2023}7,\qquad b=\log_{2023}289,\qquad t=\log_{2023}x.
\]
Then \(a+b=1\) and \(0<a,b<1\). The forbidden bases correspond to \(t=-a,-b,-1\).

By the change-of-base formula, the equation becomes
\[
\frac{1}{t+a}\cdot\frac{1}{t+b}=\frac{1}{t+1}.
\]
On the allowed domain, clearing denominators gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
(t+a)(t+b)&=t+1,\\
t^2+(a+b)t+ab&=t+1,\\
t^2&=1-ab.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(0<ab<1\), there are exactly two distinct real roots,
\[
t_1=\sqrt{1-ab},\qquad t_2=-\sqrt{1-ab}.
\]
Both are allowed: the polynomial \(t^2+ab-1\) takes the nonzero values \(-b,-a,ab\) at the excluded inputs \(-a,-b,-1\), respectively.

Each root gives one positive solution \(x=2023^t\). Their product is therefore
\[
x_1x_2=2023^{t_1}2023^{t_2}=2023^0=\boxed{1},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
